title: Date Course
text: “Well then, I'll pay off some of Zeltoble's underground organizations and see if they know anything about usaunnies.”
“Please do.”
“Either way, it's not like I'm going to go ask right away. I'll get in touch, so just wait a bit. Anyway, Motoyasu-kun,”
“What is it?”
“You've been hanging around me since yesterday looking all around nervously—what's going on?”
“I'm preparing in case an assassin comes after Father from somewhere, I say.”
“Come on, there's no way that's true... there's no one like that left in Melromarc anymore.”

Not Three Heroes Church—it's Rival. The moment I take my eyes off things, that one could still gobble Father up in a heartbeat, and that hasn't changed one bit. It's maddening that thanks to Rafumi I can't say this directly. Even if it claims it won't do anything, it's definitely lying in wait, watching for its chance. Now that it's shown itself, it's not something I can afford to let my guard down around at all. In fact, I can't stop keeping watch over where it is and what it's doing right now. I have a feeling it's only a matter of time before it sees through my countermeasures and makes its move.
“It's pretty hilarious imagining Melromarc's underworld searching frantically, bloodshot-eyed. Those guys really underestimate the Heroes.”
“That hasn't really changed since around the time of the circus incident.”
“By the way, apparently there was recently an incident in Melromarc where a circus troupe claiming to be the Shield Hero handed out food at a soup kitchen and poisoned it.”
“I mean... people really love impersonating me. Anyone who's been a few times would immediately tell it's a different circus though.”
“Of course, they say people noticed something was off from how the food stall was run and nobody bought anything. Apparently no one ate it even when it was free.”
“No matter how much people hate the Shield Hero, they're not about to volunteer as victims.”
“And that's where Sakura comes in.”
“She does seem like she'd do that... always coming up with one trick after another.”
And so, that was the story of Father and the others getting wind of Three Heroes Church's misdeeds and being appalled by them, I say.
“Boo—”
I heard Luna-chan's voice of protest. Hm!?
“What was that? Sounded like Luna-chan's voice.”

When I rushed to the scene... it seemed Luna-chan had wanted to cling to Ren, but Rival's parent had grabbed her and driven her off. Assistant was watching how things unfolded from a bit of a distance.
“Alright! I managed to fend off Luna when she came at me! Gaelion, well done chasing her off! Looks like all that careful raising is paying off!”
Ren was celebrating like he'd won, but that meant Luna-chan's defeat, and from where I stood, there was nothing remotely amusing about that!
“Gau! Nano—!”
“Boo! That Gaelion pulled some kind of new trick I haven't seen before—”
“You're saying that, but you're the one clinging onto me, Luna-chan!”

It seemed Luna-chan, having been chased off, was venting her frustration by hugging Keel. She'd failed to capture Ren. Her plan had probably been to send Keel and Ren off on a date somewhere with a nice romantic mood.
“Luna won't lose this time—Luna's going to go out with Keel-kun to get stronger—”
“Don't drag me into this, Luna-chan! Hey!”
Zudododo! With that, Luna-chan took off running, dragging Keel along with her.
“I managed to chase her off, but I guess I can't let my guard down around Luna and the others... Wyndia, make sure you give Gaelion proper instructions.”
“Y-yeah. Luna-chan's a good kid as long as it's not about Keel-kun and the others though...”

Assistant was helping in the fight against the parent possessing and impersonating Rival's body. Once the commotion settled down, Assistant and Ren each headed off to do what they wanted. Judging by the destination, it seemed Ren was headed to where Crocodile Guy was training.
“Another one of the usual lovers' spats. Looks like it ended in Ren-san's group's favor today though.”

“I've warned her that forcing things isn't okay, so Luna-chan's not gone so overboard as before... but it seems like she tries to get Keel-kun and Ren into a romantic mood by putting them on her back under the pretext of a date-drive.”
“That would be one of my supervised date courses—the one with a beautiful sunset view, or the one with gorgeous night scenery! Zeltoble has both, I say!”
Being a town with a side that never sleeps, it's beautiful all around, indeed.

“It's a town packed with plenty going on... Lars-chan going out to play and not coming home until morning was common enough that her father and grandfather had to warn her, and she made an obviously sour face about it. Though lately that same father's been getting called out to Zeltoble a lot, so ironically he doesn't want to go there anymore.”
“Which do you prefer, Father—the sunset date course or the night-view course?”

Incidentally, there was a time I once tried wooing Big Sister with slightly old-fashioned phrasing on the sunset-view course. From my research at the time, I'd learned that pigs of this world respond fairly well to somewhat old-fashioned lines. The result was that I got scolded, though. Big Sister isn't the type to be easily swayed by mood, so I found myself curious how Father managed to satisfy her on dates afterward. As for Mole, going out to places like Zeltoble with Father seems common across every world. Apparently the purpose is always to go check out the finished pieces at jewelry shops... it seems neither of them has any concept of buying precious metals as goods for trade. If they do buy any, it's for research and gets taken apart almost immediately. ...Big Sister is difficult enough, but isn't Mole's personality pretty difficult too? Just as I was thinking that, Mole—whose image had been repainted to resemble Big Sister ever since becoming a spirit—answered me just like Big Sister would, saying I had no business worrying about that. Since she shares a common template with Big Sister, it's easy to imagine, but I think Mole is properly the more soft-spoken type. Big-Sister-Mole just won't do. Time for an image repaint. In any case, my plan all along was to get Father and Mole to grow close, so that if Big Sister ever got angry, I could drag Mole down with me as a scapegoat. While I was thinking about all this...
“For some reason Theo and Wolf asked me the same thing—is this some kind of trend?”
“What did you say—!?”
That Rabbit Guy and the wolf! When did they go and ask Father about this!
“Did that lizardman fellow not ask you?”
“Shion? Ah... he talks with Eclair-san a lot, so I bet he already knows what to do about dates and stuff.”
“I don't think that's it, actually.”
“By the way, which do you prefer, Father?”
“I've gone out with Lars-chan and Sadeena-san, and with Raphtalia-chan and the others too, at that time of day—both were beautiful views.”

Father gave that carefree answer of his. If only he'd graduated straight past this stage, how much easier things would have been! Father was, without question, the oblivious type—going on dates without even realizing they were dates, all while leaving the women hanging. I could feel, painfully well, just how much Big Sister from the first world must have suffered. Oh? I feel like Big Sister from the first world is telling me I don't need to understand that, but I happen to be a considerate man, I say. In any case, given that it's already been confirmed Rival is lurking nearby, there's no time left to spare. If I don't stay properly alert, Rival might genuinely pull off a dependable-big-sister move and swoop right in for the attack. I'd like to dispose of it before Father catches on. I can't let it hand over its heart. Rival is... just where is it hiding!
“What about Itsuki? With Emia-san and Rishia-chan and all?”
“Those two? Emia-san is a Rumo-species, but she has trauma around darkness and isn't good with it, so she seems to do better at dusk. As for Rishia-san, I really can't say.”
“I-I see.”

Father remarked, “I wonder if Itsuki is dense about that kind of thing?”—said with such a straight face that I wanted to shoot back, “Look who's talking.” That's the thing, though. Perhaps whenever people get pushy with them, both Father and Itsuki end up harboring obliviousness? No... actually, Father's oblivious either way. And here he was, so interested in other people's love lives too.
